title: Luke Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 17.

questions.question: In Luke 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus said it is impossible that offences will come
The apostles asked the Lord to increase their faith
Jesus spoke about forgiving a brother seven times
Ten lepers called out to Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus said it is impossible that offences will come
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in the chapter as seen in Luke 17:1.

questions.question: What is better for someone who offends one of the little ones, according to Jesus?
options: To be hanged with a millstone and cast into the sea
To be forgiven and set free
To be punished by the elders
questions.correctAnswer: To be hanged with a millstone and cast into the sea
questions.explanation: Jesus states in Luke 17:2 that it would be better for such a person to have a millstone hung around their neck and be cast into the sea.

questions.question: What should you do if your brother trespasses against you and repents?
questions.explanation: According to Luke 17:3, if your brother repents, you should forgive him.

questions.question: How many times should you forgive your brother in a day if he repents?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:4 states that you should forgive him even if he trespasses against you seven times in a day and repents.

questions.question: What did the apostles ask the Lord to do?
questions.explanation: The apostles specifically asked the Lord to increase their faith as stated in Luke 17:5.

questions.question: What did the Lord say about faith as a grain of mustard seed?
options: It can command a sycamine tree
It is the smallest of all seeds
questions.correctAnswer: It can command a sycamine tree
questions.explanation: In Luke 17:6, the Lord mentioned that faith as a grain of mustard seed can command a sycamine tree to be plucked up and planted in the sea.

questions.question: What will a master say to his servant after he comes from the field?
options: Go and sit down to meat
Thank you for your hard work
questions.explanation: According to Luke 17:8, the master would rather say to his servant to make ready wherewith he may sup.

questions.question: Does the master thank the servant for doing what he was commanded?
options: Only if he does extra work
No, he does not thank him
questions.correctAnswer: No, he does not thank him
questions.explanation: Luke 17:9 indicates that the master does not thank the servant for doing what was commanded.

questions.question: What should the servants say after doing all that was commanded?
questions.explanation: In Luke 17:10, the servants should say that they are unprofitable servants and have done what was their duty.

questions.question: Where did Jesus pass through on His way to Jerusalem?
options: Through the land of the Philistines
questions.explanation: As mentioned in Luke 17:11, Jesus passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee on His way to Jerusalem.

questions.question: How many lepers met Jesus as He entered a certain village?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:12 states that ten men that were lepers met Jesus as He entered the village.

questions.question: Did the lepers call out to Jesus for mercy?
questions.explanation: The lepers lifted up their voices and called out to Jesus for mercy as stated in Luke 17:13.

questions.question: Jesus referred to offences as something that would NOT come.
questions.explanation: In Luke 17:1, Jesus states that it is impossible but that offences will come, indicating that they will indeed come.

questions.question: The apostles did not ask Jesus to increase their faith.
questions.explanation: The apostles explicitly asked the Lord to increase their faith as noted in Luke 17:5.

questions.question: Jesus told the apostles they should forgive only once if their brother repents.
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed that they should forgive even seven times in a day if the brother repents, as stated in Luke 17:4.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Luke 17:14, what did Jesus tell the ten lepers to do after he saw them?
options: Go shew yourselves unto the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Go shew yourselves unto the priests
questions.explanation: Luke 17:14 states, 'And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests.' This was the instruction given to the lepers after Jesus saw them.

questions.question: What does Luke 17:19 promise will happen if someone shows gratitude and faith as the healed Samaritan did in verse 17:15?
options: Thy faith hath made thee whole
questions.correctAnswer: Thy faith hath made thee whole
questions.explanation: Luke 17:19 says, 'Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole,' promising wholeness to one who shows faith and gratitude as seen in verse 15.

questions.question: Which individual among the ten healed lepers returned to glorify God according to Luke 17:15-16?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:16 states, 'And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan,' identifying the one who returned.

questions.question: How do Luke 17:20 and Luke 17:21 together describe the nature of the kingdom of God?
options: It cometh not with observation and is within you
It will be visible in the sky
It arrives with a loud trumpet
It is established through a king
questions.correctAnswer: It cometh not with observation and is within you
questions.explanation: Luke 17:20 says, 'The kingdom of God cometh not with observation,' and verse 21 adds, 'for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you,' describing its spiritual and internal nature.

questions.question: What warning does Jesus give about false claims of seeing the days of the Son of Man in Luke 17:23?
options: Go not after them, nor follow them
questions.correctAnswer: Go not after them, nor follow them
questions.explanation: Luke 17:23 instructs, 'go not after them, nor follow them,' warning against following false reports about the coming of the Son of Man.

questions.question: What comparison does Jesus make in Luke 17:24 to describe how the Son of Man will appear in his day?
options: As lightning shining from one part of heaven to the other
questions.correctAnswer: As lightning shining from one part of heaven to the other
questions.explanation: Luke 17:24 says, 'For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.'

questions.question: According to Luke 17:25, what must the Son of Man first experience before his day comes?
options: Suffer many things and be rejected
questions.correctAnswer: Suffer many things and be rejected
questions.explanation: Luke 17:25 states, 'But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation,' indicating the necessary suffering before glory.

questions.question: What parallel does Jesus draw between the days of Noah and the days of the Son of Man in Luke 17:26?
options: People were eating, drinking, marrying, and unaware until the flood came
The earth was peaceful and prosperous
questions.correctAnswer: People were eating, drinking, marrying, and unaware until the flood came
questions.explanation: Luke 17:26 references the behavior in Noah's days implying normal life continued unaware of impending judgment, which will also characterize the days of the Son of Man.

questions.question: In Luke 17:17, what question does Jesus ask after one leper returned to give thanks?
options: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
questions.correctAnswer: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:17 records Jesus asking, 'Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?' highlighting the ingratitude of the others.

questions.question: According to Luke 17:18, how many of the cleansed lepers returned to give glory to God?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:18 says, 'There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger,' emphasizing the singular grateful one.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith does Jesus teach in Luke 17:6 that connects to the healing of the lepers?
options: Faith as a grain of mustard seed can move mountains
Faith must be proven by works only
questions.correctAnswer: Faith as a grain of mustard seed can move mountains
questions.explanation: Luke 17:6 explains that even faith as small as a mustard seed can result in extraordinary outcomes, like commanding a tree to be uprooted, which connects to the healing power shown to the lepers.

questions.question: What attitude toward forgiveness does Luke 17:3-4 teach that can be applied to Christian living?
options: Forgive a brother even if he sins against you seven times a day and repents
Hold grudges until full restitution is made
questions.correctAnswer: Forgive a brother even if he sins against you seven times a day and repents
questions.explanation: Luke 17:4 says, 'If he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him,' teaching persistent forgiveness.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about a servant's duty in Luke 17:10 and how does it relate to Christian service?
options: We are unprofitable servants who have only done our duty
We deserve praise for every task
questions.correctAnswer: We are unprofitable servants who have only done our duty
questions.explanation: Luke 17:10 teaches humility by stating that after doing all commanded, servants should say, 'We are unprofitable servants,' emphasizing duty over reward.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 17:20, the kingdom of God will be visibly established with signs and wonders.
questions.explanation: Luke 17:20 states, 'The kingdom of God cometh not with observation,' indicating it is not visibly established with signs and wonders.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the ten lepers to stay where they were until He returned to heal them.
questions.explanation: Luke 17:14 says Jesus told them, 'Go shew yourselves unto the priests,' which implies they were to go and show themselves rather than wait for Him.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 17.

questions.question: What did people do until the day Noah entered the ark?
questions.explanation: They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all. (Luke 17:27)

questions.question: What happened on the same day Lot went out of Sodom?
options: Fire and brimstone rained from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Fire and brimstone rained from heaven
questions.explanation: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all. (Luke 17:29)

questions.question: In the day when the Son of Man is revealed, what should a person on the housetop do?
options: Come down to take his stuff
questions.explanation: In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away. (Luke 17:31)

questions.question: What lesson is illustrated by remembering Lot's wife?
questions.explanation: Remember Lot's wife. (Luke 17:32) illustrates the importance of not looking back to a life of sin when called to follow God.

questions.question: What will happen to the one who seeks to save his life?
questions.explanation: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it. (Luke 17:33)

questions.question: What will happen to two men in one bed according to Jesus?
options: One shall be taken, the other left
questions.correctAnswer: One shall be taken, the other left
questions.explanation: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left. (Luke 17:34)

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'eagles' in Luke 17:37 refer to?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'eagles' (aetos) refers to birds of prey that gather around a carcass, illustrating a gathering for judgment.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Luke 17:30, 'Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed'?
questions.explanation: This verse foreshadows the events of the end times and the return of Christ, linking past judgments to future events.

questions.question: Which passage connects to Luke 17:26 regarding the days of Noah?
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:37-39 connects to the theme of judgment in the days of Noah, illustrating how people were unaware until it was too late.

questions.question: Which passage connects to Luke 17:29 about Lot's departure from Sodom?
questions.explanation: Genesis 19:25-26 recounts the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah when Lot departed, directly connecting to Luke 17:29.

questions.question: What comes before Luke 17:32, 'Remember Lot's wife'?
questions.explanation: The context leading to Luke 17:32 involves a warning about judgment and the consequences of looking back.

questions.question: What comes after Luke 17:36, regarding the men in the field?
options: The return of the Son of Man
The parable of the lost sheep
questions.explanation: After Luke 17:36, Jesus answers the disciples' question about where the taken will go, explaining it with the image of eagles.

questions.question: The phrase 'the kingdom of God is within you' emphasizes what aspect of the kingdom?
questions.explanation: The kingdom of God is within you emphasizes the spiritual presence of God's reign in the hearts of believers. (Luke 17:21)

questions.question: In Luke 17, Jesus emphasizes forgiveness how many times?
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes forgiveness multiple times, especially in Luke 17:3-4, which illustrates the importance of forgiving others.

questions.question: According to Luke 17, those who are unprofitable servants deserve praise.
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that they are to consider themselves unprofitable servants, indicating they do not deserve praise for fulfilling their duty. (Luke 17:10)

theological.title: Luke Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 17:3 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification requires mutual accountability and forgiveness among believers
Sanctification is a one-time event without ongoing responsibility
Sanctification depends solely on external rituals
Sanctification excludes the need for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification requires mutual accountability and forgiveness among believers
questions.explanation: Luke 17:3 instructs believers to rebuke a trespassing brother and forgive him if he repents, highlighting the ongoing process of sanctification involving accountability and forgiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith is taught in Luke 17:6?
options: Even faith as small as a mustard seed can accomplish great works
Faith must be large and visible to be effective
Faith is irrelevant to divine power
questions.correctAnswer: Even faith as small as a mustard seed can accomplish great works
questions.explanation: Luke 17:6 explains that faith as small as a mustard seed can command a sycamine tree to be uprooted and obey, emphasizing the power of even minimal genuine faith.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of human service and duty is taught in Luke 17:10?
options: Believers are unprofitable servants who only do their duty
Believers earn special merit through their works
Servants deserve praise for obeying masters
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are unprofitable servants who only do their duty
questions.explanation: Luke 17:10 teaches that after doing all commanded things, believers must recognize themselves as unprofitable servants, emphasizing humility and the proper understanding of works in salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 17:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Luke 17:13 the ten lepers cry out to Jesus, 'Master, have mercy on us,' demonstrating His attribute of mercy in responding to their plea.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 17:19 reveal in Jesus' response to the healed Samaritan?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:19 reveals Jesus' faithfulness by acknowledging the Samaritan’s faith and affirming, 'thy faith hath made thee whole,' showing God's reliable response to faith.

questions.question: How does Luke 17:20-21 connect to broader biblical teaching on the Kingdom of God?
options: The Kingdom of God is a present spiritual reality within believers
The Kingdom of God is primarily a political kingdom to be established visibly
The Kingdom of God is limited to geographic Jerusalem
The Kingdom of God will come only through violent revolution
questions.correctAnswer: The Kingdom of God is a present spiritual reality within believers
questions.explanation: Luke 17:20-21 teaches that the Kingdom of God 'is within you,' emphasizing its present spiritual nature rather than a visible, external political kingdom, aligning with New Testament theology.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Luke 17:26-30 develop through the comparison of Noah and Lot’s days?
options: Judgment will come suddenly and unexpectedly upon the ungodly
God’s judgment depends on human works alone
Salvation is guaranteed to all by heritage
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment will come suddenly and unexpectedly upon the ungodly
questions.explanation: Luke 17:26-30 illustrates how the days of Noah and Lot ended in sudden judgment, teaching that the coming of the Son of man’s day will similarly be sudden and unexpected.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 17:1 and Luke 17:2 teach about human sin and its consequences?
options: Offenses are inevitable but causing others to sin is severely condemned
Sin can be avoided entirely by human effort
Offenses are trivial and without consequence
Causing others to sin is a minor fault
questions.correctAnswer: Offenses are inevitable but causing others to sin is severely condemned
questions.explanation: Luke 17:1 warns that offenses will come, but Luke 17:2 emphasizes the severity of causing 'little ones' to stumble, condemning such offenses with hyperbolic imagery of a millstone around the neck.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 17:4 and Luke 17:5 teach about faith and forgiveness?
options: Forgiveness must be extended repeatedly and faith empowers this grace
Forgiveness is limited and faith is irrelevant
Faith negates the need for forgiveness
Forgiveness depends on human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness must be extended repeatedly and faith empowers this grace
questions.explanation: Luke 17:4 commands forgiving a brother who repents multiple times, and Luke 17:5 shows the apostles asking Jesus to increase their faith, linking faith to the capacity to forgive continually.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 17:11-14 and Luke 17:15-19 teach about salvation and gratitude?
options: Salvation is a gracious gift and true faith expresses itself through thanksgiving
Salvation is earned by works and gratitude is optional
Only chosen ethnic groups receive salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is a gracious gift and true faith expresses itself through thanksgiving
questions.explanation: The healing of ten lepers in Luke 17:11-14 shows salvation as a gift, while the one Samaritan’s return to thank Jesus in Luke 17:15-19 exemplifies that genuine faith includes grateful worship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Luke 17:22-24 denies any visible coming of Christ. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The coming of the Son of man will be unmistakably visible like lightning across the sky
The coming of Christ is purely spiritual and invisible
The coming of Christ will be secret and unknown
questions.correctAnswer: The coming of the Son of man will be unmistakably visible like lightning across the sky
questions.explanation: Luke 17:24 compares the Son of man’s coming to lightning shining across the sky, indicating a sudden and visible event, contrary to sceptical claims denying visibility.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment does Luke 17:31-32 teach?
options: Urgency in obeying God without delay, illustrated by the command to not look back as Lot’s wife did
God delays judgment to allow repentance
Salvation is based on possessions and earthly security
Judgment is arbitrary and without warning
questions.correctAnswer: Urgency in obeying God without delay, illustrated by the command to not look back as Lot’s wife did
questions.explanation: Luke 17:31-32 warns not to return for possessions during judgment and commands remembering Lot’s wife, who looked back and was lost, emphasizing urgent obedience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Luke 17:25 regarding the Son of man’s mission?
questions.explanation: Luke 17:25 reveals that the Son of man must first suffer and be rejected, highlighting the divine attribute of the Suffering Servant as part of God’s redemptive plan.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical significance does Luke 17:36-37 imply about the gathering of the elect?
options: The gathering will be sovereign and certain wherever the dead body is, symbolized by eagles
The elect will gather by human effort alone
The gathering is metaphorical and unimportant
There will be no final gathering of the elect
questions.correctAnswer: The gathering will be sovereign and certain wherever the dead body is, symbolized by eagles
questions.explanation: Luke 17:37 shows Jesus’ response that 'where the body is, there the eagles will be gathered,' symbolizing the sovereign and inevitable gathering of the elect at judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about human life and salvation is taught in Luke 17:33?
options: Those who seek to save their life will lose it, but those who lose their life will preserve it
Life is saved through works alone
questions.correctAnswer: Those who seek to save their life will lose it, but those who lose their life will preserve it
questions.explanation: Luke 17:33 teaches the paradoxical doctrine that true life and salvation come through self-denial and surrender, not through self-preservation.
